tools.name: json_format
tools.description: Pretty-print a JSON document with consistent indentation, optionally sorting object keys alphabetically at every level (useful before diffing two documents). Fails with the line and column of the first syntax error if the input is not valid JSON.

tools.name: json_validate
tools.description: Check whether text is valid JSON (RFC 8259). Returns valid=true with the top-level type, total key count and nesting depth, or valid=false with the error message and its exact line and column. Use this to find why a payload will not parse.

tools.name: json_minify
tools.description: Remove all insignificant whitespace from a JSON document, producing the smallest equivalent text. Reports the size reduction. Fails with line and column if the input is not valid JSON.

tools.name: json_escape
tools.description: Escape raw text so it can be embedded as a JSON string value (quotes, backslashes, newlines, control characters), or unescape an escaped JSON string back to raw text. The result does not include the surrounding double quotes.

tools.name: csv_to_json
tools.description: Parse CSV text with a header row into an array of JSON objects, one per row. Handles quoted fields, embedded commas and newlines, and converts numeric and boolean cells to their JSON types.

tools.name: json_to_csv
tools.description: Convert a JSON array of flat objects into CSV text with a header row. Fields containing commas, quotes or newlines are quoted correctly.

tools.name: yaml_to_json
tools.description: Parse a YAML document and return it as JSON. Reports the line of the first syntax error — useful for debugging indentation problems in Kubernetes manifests, CI configs and Compose files.

tools.name: json_to_yaml
tools.description: Convert a JSON document to block-style YAML with 2-space indentation.

tools.name: geojson_validate
tools.description: Validate a GeoJSON document against RFC 7946: geometry types, coordinate array shapes, longitude/latitude ranges, closed polygon rings and Feature/FeatureCollection structure. Returns every violation found.

tools.name: format_code
tools.description: Re-indent and beautify SQL, CSS, HTML or XML source. Use it to make minified or single-line code readable before reviewing or diffing it.

tools.name: text_diff
tools.description: Compare two texts line by line and return a unified diff plus counts of added, removed, changed and unchanged lines. Deterministic — use it instead of eyeballing whether two configs, prompts or files differ.

tools.name: base64
tools.description: Encode UTF-8 text to Base64, or decode Base64 back to text. Supports the URL-safe alphabet (RFC 4648 §5) and tolerates missing padding when decoding. Use this rather than computing Base64 by hand, which models get wrong on anything longer than a few bytes.

tools.name: url_encode
tools.description: Percent-encode text for use in a URL, or decode a percent-encoded string. In component mode (default) every reserved character is encoded, which is what a query-string value needs; with component=false the URL structure (:/?#&=) is preserved.

tools.name: jwt_decode
tools.description: Decode a JSON Web Token into its header and payload, and convert the iat/nbf/exp claims to ISO timestamps with an expired flag. Decoding only: the signature is NOT verified, so never treat the result as proof the token is authentic.

tools.name: hash
tools.description: Compute the SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 digest of UTF-8 text, as hex or Base64. Use it to produce checksums, cache keys or integrity values — a model cannot compute a real hash without a tool.

tools.name: number_base_convert
tools.description: Convert an integer between binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal. Arbitrary precision, so 64-bit and larger values convert exactly (no floating-point rounding).

tools.name: color_convert
tools.description: Convert a colour between hex, RGB and HSL, and report its WCAG contrast ratio against white and black so you can tell which text colour is legible on it.

tools.name: timestamp_convert
tools.description: Convert between Unix epoch time and ISO 8601. Accepts epoch seconds or milliseconds (detected by magnitude) or any ISO 8601 date-time, and returns all forms plus the weekday. Call it with no arguments to get the current UTC time — a model has no clock of its own.

tools.name: uuid_generate
tools.description: Generate one or more UUIDs. Version 7 (default) is time-ordered and sorts chronologically, which makes it the better choice for database primary keys; version 4 is fully random. Use this whenever a real, unique identifier is needed — a model-invented UUID is neither random nor unique.

tools.name: date_diff
tools.description: Compute the exact span between two dates: total days, weeks and days, a calendar breakdown in years, months and days, and the number of business days (Monday to Friday; public holidays are not known). Leap years and month lengths are handled. Use it for ages, deadlines, contract terms and "how long

tools.name: date_add
tools.description: Add or subtract years, months, weeks, days or business days from a date and return the resulting date and weekday. Month arithmetic clamps to the end of the month (31 January plus one month is the last day of February). Business days skip Saturdays and Sundays; public holidays are not known. Use neg

tools.name: timezone_convert
tools.description: Convert a date and time from one IANA time zone to another, applying the daylight-saving rules in force on that date in each zone. Returns the local time, UTC offset and weekday in both zones and the UTC instant. Flags local times that occur twice or not at all around a clock change. Use it for meet

tools.name: cron_explain
tools.description: Parse a standard 5-field cron expression (or an @daily-style macro), describe in words when it fires, and compute its next run times in UTC. Use it to check a schedule before deploying it — computing cron fire times by reasoning alone is error-prone, especially with day-of-month and day-of-week both

tools.name: regex_test
tools.description: Run a JavaScript (ECMAScript) regular expression against text and return every match with its index and capture groups. Use it to verify a pattern actually matches what you intend before putting it in code. Reports a syntax error if the pattern does not compile.

tools.name: cidr_calculate
tools.description: Given an IPv4 CIDR block (e.g. 10.0.0.0/22), return its network and broadcast addresses, subnet and wildcard masks, usable host range and host count, and whether it is private (RFC 1918). Optionally split it into equal smaller subnets. IPv4 only.

tools.name: http_headers_analyze
tools.description: Parse raw HTTP response headers (as printed by `curl -I`) and audit them: explains each header, flags risky values (weak CSP, cookies missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite, permissive CORS), lists the security headers that are missing, and gives a 0–100 score.

tools.name: llm_models
tools.description: List current large-language-model API offerings with list prices (USD per 1M input/output tokens), long-context surcharge rules, context window and max output. Covers OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, Mistral and Meta. Each response states the date the prices were last verified against the p

tools.name: llm_cost_estimate
tools.description: Calculate what an LLM workload costs: tokens per request × requests, at list price, with long-context surcharges applied correctly (several providers bill the whole request at a higher rate once the prompt passes a threshold). Name a model for one figure, or omit it to get every model ranked cheapes

tools.name: llm_price_changes
tools.description: Return the dated record of LLM API price changes, model launches, deprecations and shutdown dates, plus the computed differences between the dates the price list was re-verified. Each announced event carries the provider page it came from. Use it to answer "did the price of X change?", "when does mo

tools.name: count_tokens
tools.description: Count how many tokens a piece of text uses. Exact for OpenAI's published o200k_base encoding; for Anthropic and Google models it returns the estimate from each provider's documented ratio, labelled as an estimate. Use it to check a prompt fits a context window or to feed llm_cost_estimate.

tools.name: llm_stream_assemble
tools.description: Reassemble a raw streamed LLM API response (server-sent events) into the message it adds up to: text, reasoning, tool calls with parsed arguments, stop reason and token usage. Understands Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions (and compatible providers), OpenAI Responses, Gemini generateContent

tools.name: ucp_profile_validate
tools.description: Validate a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) profile document — the JSON a store publishes at /.well-known/ucp, or the profile an agent platform advertises — against the UCP specification: version format, required registries, service bindings and endpoints, capability entries and orphaned extensions

tools.name: product_feed_validate
tools.description: Validate a product feed written for OpenAI's product feed schema (the format ChatGPT shopping ingests) row by row: the eleven required fields, the accepted availability values, the "amount CURRENCY" price format, URLs, GTIN length and check digit, duplicate item IDs, variant groups, checkout fields

tools.name: http_signature_verify
tools.description: Verify the signature on an HTTP request, response or webhook and explain a failure. Handles RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures with RFC 9530 Content-Digest (the scheme UCP uses) for ecdsa-p256-sha256, ecdsa-p384-sha384, ed25519, hmac-sha256, rsa-pss-sha512 and rsa-v1_5-sha256, and the ACP order-webhoo

tools.description: Decode an SD-JWT or SD-JWT VC (RFC 9901 selective-disclosure JWT, the credential format of the EU Digital Identity Wallet and of agent payment mandates): split the issuer-signed JWT, the disclosures and the key-binding JWT; hash each disclosure and match it to the digest that references it; rebuild

tools.name: india_id_validate
tools.description: Check Indian identifiers by structure and check digit: GSTIN (state code, embedded PAN, check character), PAN, TAN, IFSC, Aadhaar (Verhoeff check digit), CIN and Udyam registration numbers. Pass one identifier or many, one per line; the type is detected unless given. Returns whether each is well-for

tools.name: payment_qr_decode
tools.description: Decode the text inside a payment QR code or payment link and check it: EMVCo merchant-presented codes (the tag-length-value format behind Pix, PromptPay, DuitNow, BharatQR, PayNow, QRIS and others) with the CRC recomputed and mandatory fields checked, UPI payment links (upi://pay?…), the SEPA credit

tools.name: ach_file_validate
tools.description: Parse a US ACH file in the NACHA fixed-width format (94 characters per record) and check it: record order and nesting, entry and addenda counts, the entry hash, debit and credit totals at batch and file level, the block count and padding, routing-number check digits, transaction and service class co

tools.name: aba_routing_check
tools.description: Check a nine-digit US ABA routing (transit) number: the check-digit rule, with the weighted sum shown, and what the first two digits indicate (Federal Reserve district, thrift, electronic or traveler's cheque series). Checks the number only; it does not say whether the number is assigned to a bank.

tools.name: iso20022_read
tools.description: Read an ISO 20022 XML payment message as plain payments and check it. Interprets pain.001 (credit transfer initiation), pain.008 (direct debit), pain.002 and pacs.002 (status reports), pacs.008 (interbank credit transfer), pacs.004 (return), camt.052/053/054 (account reports, statements, notificatio

tools.name: einvoice_read

Handles European EN 16931 invoices in UBL (Invoice, CreditNote) and UN/CEFACT CII syntax — the formats XRechnung, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0, Factur-X and ZUGFeRD carry — and Indian GST e-invoices (the invoice JSON sent to the Invoice Regi

tools.name: loan_payment
tools.description: Compute the fixed monthly payment on an amortising loan or mortgage (the EMI), plus total interest and total repaid, using the standard annuity formula. Optionally returns the first months of the amortisation schedule showing the interest/principal split. Use it instead of estimating — compounding m

tools.name: compound_interest
tools.description: Project the future value of a lump sum with compound interest, optionally with a fixed contribution added at the end of every month (a savings plan or SIP). Returns the final value, total contributed, interest earned and a year-by-year balance.

tools.name: cagr
tools.description: Compute the compound annual growth rate (CAGR) between a starting and ending value over a number of years — the single constant yearly rate that would produce the same result. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: json_validate, base64, count_tokens, ucp_profile_validate, product_feed_validate, iso20022_read · Private data: json_format, json_minify, yaml_to_json, json_to_yaml, geojson_validate, text_diff, jwt_decode, uuid_generate, cidr_calculate, llm_models, llm_cost_estimate, llm_price_changes, count_tokens, llm_stream_assemble, ucp_profile_validate, product_feed_validate, http_signature_verify, sd_jwt_decode, ach_file_validate, einvoice_read · Public sink: cidr_calculate, product_feed_validate, http_signature_verify, sd_jwt_decode · Destructive: json_format, json_minify, format_code, cron_explain, regex_test, ucp_profile_validate, product_feed_validate, sd_jwt_decode, india_id_validate, payment_qr_decode, ach_file_validate, einvoice_read.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: json_validate, base64, count_tokens, ucp_profile_validate, product_feed_validate, iso20022_read · Private data: json_format, json_minify, yaml_to_json, json_to_yaml, geojson_validate, text_diff, jwt_decode, uuid_generate, cidr_calculate, llm_models, llm_cost_estimate, llm_price_changes, count_tokens, llm_stream_assemble, ucp_profile_validate, product_feed_validate, http_signature_verify, sd_jwt_decode, ach_file_validate, einvoice_read · Public sink: cidr_calculate, product_feed_validate, http_signature_verify, sd_jwt_decode · Destructive: json_format, json_minify, format_code, cron_explain, regex_test, ucp_profile_validate, product_feed_validate, sd_jwt_decode, india_id_validate, payment_qr_decode, ach_file_validate, einvoice_read

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
